questions.question: Why do animals have adaptations?
options: To reduce the total gene pool
To prevent decomposers from recycling nutrients
To help them survive in their environment
To eliminate producers from food chains

questions.question: Which feature is an example of a physical adaptation in animals?
options: Being nocturnal
Thick fur
Migrating south in winter
Hibernating through winter

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a behavioural adaptation in animals?
options: Thick fur
Sharp claws
Being nocturnal
Shallow roots

questions.question: Why is maintaining biodiversity important in an ecosystem?
options: It helps to maintain healthy habitats.
It eliminates the need for producers.
It reduces the size of all gene pools.
It stops the flow of energy through food chains.

questions.question: What is meant by the term 'gene pool'?
options: The total biomass at the bottom of a pyramid
The range of DNA in a species
The physical surroundings of an ecosystem
A non-living component of a habitat

questions.question: Which set of methods can be used to maintain biodiversity?
options: Conservation, protection and gene banks
Deforestation, urbanisation and sampling
Random sampling, bias and harvesting
Interdependence, biomass and decay

questions.question: Why do scientists use sampling methods to estimate population sizes in an area?
options: Because quadrats can only measure biomass
Because it would be impossible to count all the organisms
Because sampling stops environmental change
Because classification keys require sampling first

questions.question: What are quadrats used to sample?
options: Fast-flying birds
Large swimming fish
Plants or slow-moving animals
Substances recycled by decomposers

questions.question: Why is most sampling with quadrats carried out randomly?
options: To avoid bias in your results
To increase the biomass of the area
To count every single organism
To change the physical environment

questions.question: What can classification keys be used for?
options: To estimate total biomass
To identify different species
To store gene pools safely
To measure sunlight levels

questions.question: What makes up an ecosystem?
options: Only the non-living surroundings in a given area
A community of organisms interacting with each other and their non-living surroundings
A single species living in isolation
Only the producers in a food chain

questions.question: Why are organisms in an ecosystem described as interdependent?
options: They all have identical physical adaptations.
They do not interact with non-living surroundings.
They depend upon each other for the things they need to survive.
They produce their own biomass without energy.

questions.question: Why do all organisms in a food chain depend upon producers?
options: To break down dead material
To avoid random sampling
To make the food that moves through food chains
To provide a range of DNA

questions.question: What vital role do decomposers play for all living organisms?
options: They make food using sunlight.
They break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse.
They act as producers at the bottom of food chains.
They prevent adaptations from developing.

questions.question: What is biodiversity?
options: A measure of the range of living organisms
The total mass of non-living surroundings
The movement of light towards plants
The total number of food chains in a quadrat

questions.question: Which of these is a physical adaptation in plants used to deter consumers?
options: Growing towards light
Being nocturnal
The presence of spines
Recycling dead material

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a behavioural adaptation in plants?
options: Having deep roots
Growing towards light
Having sharp spines
Having thick bark

questions.question: What is biomass?
options: The number of species identified with a key
The mass of living material in one or more organisms
The range of DNA present in a population
The non-living surroundings of an organism

questions.question: What do pyramids of biomass show?
options: The number of dead organisms broken down by decomposers
The range of DNA found across different species
The biomass of organisms at each stage in a food chain
The speed at which plants grow towards light

questions.question: Where is the producer located in a pyramid of biomass?
options: At the top
In the middle
At the bottom
Outside the pyramid
